column1: # inventory-replica.tsv - whitespace/tab separated; '#' starts a comment (inline too)
# Read by ct-replica.sh AND ct-failback.sh. NOT ct-migrate.sh - see
# inventory-migrate.sample.tsv, whose columns mean entirely different things.
# columns:  src_ctid  [fields in ANY order]
#   src_ctid : CT to replicate. Must exist somewhere in the cluster; the
#              engine finds its node and its SOURCE storage from /etc/pve.
#   then each extra field is classified by what it IS:
#     a NUMBER              -> tgt_ctid  (default: src_ctid + OFFSET)
#     a key from BKP_DESTS  -> dest      (default: DEFAULT_DEST) - hdd / ssd
#     anything else         -> SOURCE storage assertion: the engine derives
#                              the real storage from the CT's own rootfs
#                              line; if the assertion differs, the row FAILS
#                              LOUDLY instead of silently syncing a CT that
#                              someone moved.
#   an unclassifiable field, a repeated field kind, a duplicate src_ctid, or
#   two rows resolving to the same target VMID refuse the WHOLE file - the
#   engine runs nothing (exit 2) until the inventory is fixed.
#   What you never write here: node names, paths, sizes - all derived live
#   from PVE, so there is nothing to keep in sync by hand.
# dest picks which backup pool receives the copy (see BKP_DESTS in ctrep.conf):
#   hdd -> replica-hdd/ct (capacity)     ssd -> replica-ssd/ct (fast DR start)
# Changing dest AFTER the copy exists trips GUARD R8 on purpose - move or
# destroy the old copy first, the engine will not silently split it.
# lanes: run one cron per SOURCE storage; the engine sorts each CT into its
# lane by the CT's real storage - a row does not choose its lane, its rootfs
# does:
#   ct-replica.sh --storage tank-hdd-nas
#   ct-replica.sh --storage tank-ssd-nas
# examples:
# src_ctid  [tgt_ctid]  [storage-assert]  [dest]      (extras in ANY order)
105                                       ssd
113         8113        tank-ssd-nas      ssd
114                                       # -> tgt 8114, dest DEFAULT_DEST
